title: Quarterly Review: Q3 2026
notes: Max loss: the loss if every stop is hit (the premium, for options).
Expected P&L: each trade's six-month P&L in each scenario (capped at the target, floored at the stop, options at expiry, carry excluded), weighted by its theme's probabilities.
Each theme's scenarios are separate, so combinations across themes are illustrative, not a joint model.

interactions.text: Themes 1 and 2 are negatively correlated by design: the full cycle that costs Theme 1 £1.4m is Theme 2's best outcome. Together they make money in every natural pairing of their scenarios (+£0.5m to +£6.3m).
Theme 2's loss is offset by Theme 1 (one-and-done) and Theme 3 (Bund calls).

interactions.lead: Themes 3 and 4 are opposite bets on Europe:
interactions.text: a French crisis is what derails the revival.
a burst rallies rates, which helps Themes 1 and 3 and hurts Themes 2 and 4.

interactions.lead: Themes 6 and 7 are a dollar view in two pieces:
interactions.text: debasement weakens the dollar, which is Theme 7's best scenario. Both also make money in Theme 5's burst, through the steepener, gold and the yen.
is a hawkish US status quo: France calms, the AI boom continues, the dollar holds and the BoJ stalls. That is about −£2.5m, and only Themes 1 and 2 pay. This is the book's main open risk.

themes.name: Gradual, short BoE hiking cycle, with heavy gilt supply in the belly
themes.headline: Weighted terminal ≈ 4.35% against ~4.88% priced: ~50bp too much hiking, with the skew in our favour. The belly stays cheap except in a growth break.

scenarios.name: Gradual and short
scenarios.detail: Terminal 4.25% (Nov, Feb). Oil stabilises; wages cool

scenarios.name: Full cycle
scenarios.detail: Terminal 4.75–5.00%. Hormuz stays shut; services and wages re-accelerate

scenarios.name: One and done
scenarios.detail: Terminal 3.75–4.00%, cuts H2 2027. US–Iran deal; unemployment rises

scenarios.name: Fiscal stress
scenarios.detail: ~4.50%, then pause. Headroom < £10bn; LDI-style selloff

themes.name: Inflation persistence, with domestic pressures re-accelerating (UK, euro area, G10)
themes.headline: Broad persistence is a 25% risk, but breakevens and the Brent curve price the shock fading. The long end stays anchored, so all the trades sit in the front end.

scenarios.name: Shock fades
scenarios.detail: Energy reverses (US–Iran deal) or demand destruction; no second-round effects

scenarios.name: Contained plateau
scenarios.detail: Energy stays high; headline peaks early 2027; second-round effects contained

scenarios.name: Euro-area-led
scenarios.detail: Energy stays high; euro area services ≥ 3.3% and wages respond

scenarios.name: Broad persistence
scenarios.detail: Energy stays high plus a winter gas spike; G10-wide second-round effects

themes.name: Euro area fiscal crisis, with the political risk premium rising
themes.headline: Much of the premium rise has already happened. The base case is a grind wider into the spring 2027 election, so the trades lean on relative value and convexity, with only a small outright widener.

scenarios.name: Muddle through
scenarios.detail: Budget passes in some form; ratings hold. OAT–Bund 105bp

scenarios.name: Grind wider
scenarios.detail: Budget forced through or delayed; a downgrade; election premium builds. OAT–Bund 150bp

scenarios.name: Crisis
scenarios.detail: Government falls or budget fails; contagion to Italy and Belgium. OAT–Bund 190bp

scenarios.name: Shock fades
scenarios.detail: Energy reverses; ECB hikes priced out; spreads compress. OAT–Bund 95bp

trades.name: French bank CDS vs iTraxx Senior Financials

themes.name: Euro area fiscal and growth revival (German fiscal expansion, rotation out of the US, Ukraine resolution)
themes.headline: A revival is a 25% scenario, but pricing treats it as close to zero. The curve flattened and EUR fell for cyclical reasons, so the payoff is asymmetric.

scenarios.name: Revival takes hold
scenarios.detail: German GDP > 1%; inflows return. EURUSD 1.20, 5s30s 85bp

scenarios.name: Slow burn
scenarios.detail: Spending lands slowly; energy offsets it. EURUSD 1.13

scenarios.name: Derailed
scenarios.detail: Energy deepens; French crisis; US exceptionalism returns. EURUSD 1.08

scenarios.name: Peace dividend
scenarios.detail: Ukraine deal; gas falls; reconstruction. EURUSD 1.17, 5s30s 95bp

themes.name: The AI bubble bursts
themes.headline: A burst is a 20% risk over six months, but pricing treats it as remote. Credit is the weak link because the buildout is debt-funded; the Fed's response turns an equity event into a rates trade.

scenarios.name: Boom continues
scenarios.detail: Capex guided higher; earnings beat. Nasdaq +10%, Fed hikes in December

scenarios.name: Correction
scenarios.detail: Capex digestion; rates and energy bite. Nasdaq −10%, Fed pauses

scenarios.name: Burst
scenarios.detail: A hyperscaler cuts capex. Nasdaq −30%, cuts by Q1 2027

scenarios.name: Burst, with a credit event
scenarios.detail: A data-centre financing fails. Nasdaq −40%, IG 190bp

themes.name: Dollar debasement (Fed capture, fiscal dominance, reserves moving out of dollars)
themes.headline: Debasement is a 50% scenario over six months, but the market prices a hawkish Fed and a firm dollar. If it takes hold, the front end rallies while the long end sells off and gold rallies.

scenarios.name: Dollar holds
scenarios.detail: Hikes in December; Cook stays. 2s30s 55bp, gold $3,950

scenarios.name: Slow debasement
scenarios.detail: Pauses after December under pressure; deficits widen. 2s30s 85bp, gold $4,550

scenarios.name: Capture
scenarios.detail: Cook removed; a board majority pushes cuts by Q1 2027. 2s30s 175bp, gold $5,200

scenarios.name: Growth shock
scenarios.detail: Cuts on the data, not politics (Theme 5's burst). 2s30s 120bp

themes.name: BoJ normalisation, with Japanese money coming home
themes.headline: The BoJ is hiking, but the yen hasn't followed. Intervention caps USDJPY at ~165, while steady hikes, a Fed that stops hiking or a risk-off move all take it lower: the payoff is skewed to a stronger yen.

scenarios.name: Steady normalisation
scenarios.detail: Hikes in December and April, to 1.75%. USDJPY 150

scenarios.name: BoJ stalls
scenarios.detail: On hold at 1.25%. USDJPY 161

scenarios.name: Disorderly repricing
scenarios.detail: Hikes to 2% by mid-2027; money comes home. USDJPY 140

scenarios.name: Global risk-off
scenarios.detail: Pauses; the yen rallies as a haven (Theme 5's burst). USDJPY 145
